title: δίδωμι; the Second Aorist of γινώσκω
description: The -μι conjugation: δίδωμι, the second aorist ἔγνων, the article as a pronoun before μέν and δέ, and first aorist endings on second aorist stems.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html:
Greek has one other conjugation besides the ω verbs: the μι verbs, named from the ending of δίδωμι, I give. They differ from ω verbs only in the present system and the second aorist; the other principal parts are regular: δίδωμι, δώσω, ἔδωκα, δέδωκα, δέδομαι, ἐδόθην (the aorist passive does not lengthen the stem vowel). The stem is δο-. The present system prefixes the reduplication δι- and adds the endings directly, with no variable vowel; the stem vowel is long in the singular of the indicative (δίδωμι, δίδομεν). The aorist active is first aorist in the indicative (ἔδωκα, with κ instead of σ) and second aorist in the other moods (δῶ, δός, δοῦναι, δούς).

γινώσκω is an ω verb with a second aorist of the μι form: ἔγνων, ἔγνως, ἔγνω, ἔγνωμεν, ἔγνωτε, ἔγνωσαν; subjunctive γνῶ, γνῷς, γνῷ; imperative γνῶθι, γνώτω; infinitive γνῶναι; participle γνούς.

Before μέν or δέ the article can stand alone as a pronoun: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν, but he said; οἱ δὲ ἐποίησαν οὐδέν, but they did nothing. This is different from οἱ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ or ὁ λύων, where the article is an ordinary article. An aorist participle can denote the same act as the main verb: ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν, he answered and said. Some second aorists take first aorist endings: εἶπαν beside εἶπον, εἰπόν beside εἰπέ.

ζάω has η where α would be expected in the present: ζῇς, ζῇ. ὁράω is the present of the verb whose other parts are ὄψομαι, εἶδον, ἑώρακα, ὤφθην; the common present for seeing is βλέπω.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: δῶ, δῷς, δῷ (aorist subjunctive) and διδῶ, διδῷς (present subjunctive) differ only in the reduplication; ἔδωκα looks like a perfect because of the κ, but it is the aorist (the perfect is δέδωκα). δός is give!, δούς having given. ἔγνων is an aorist (I knew, I came to know), ἔγνωκα a perfect. ὁ δέ at the start of a clause is but he, not the.
